pillar_reactions.evidence: Pre-sold on the modality and on Trevor specifically after two years of following the page: 'i like a stance on mastering the basics... i want to master the kettlebell and i feel like trevor would be the right fit', and 'I feel like he really does have the most straightforward page in like philosophy on Instagram.' Tied the mobility pillar to his own long-standing fear before it was presented — stopping training historically because his shoulders and pecs stiffened — and volunteered a plan to convert his empty carport into a kettlebell gym.

Agreed and extended the argument himself rather than questioning it: 'your cells are created by what you eat, so if you're eating sludge, your cells are actually fueled on sludge, so if you're eating clean, I feel like your system's just going to be that much cleaner.' Understood, agreed, no questions. Worth noting the rep followed with an unusually personal framing — 'it's almost like a spiritual thing for me... so much connection to what's true' — which was accepted without comment.

This is the pillar he bought, and he said so mid-delivery. On weekly check-ins and data tracking: 'See, that's, that's what I was waiting to hear. That's what I'm really looking for is that someone that knows the data and like help me keep track of it.' On 24/7 support: 'That's what I'm looking for, man. Appreciate it.' He had opened the call naming accountability as the headline need and closed the objection with it too — 'my biggest thing is I just want that accountability. I want someone that's kind of in your corner. I don't have that around me.'

anchors.raw: I've even tried some of Trevor's workouts that he posts, you know, and I've stuck with it for a couple weeks. And I did get good results.
anchors.note: The company's own free content had already produced results for this prospect once. Combined with the wider information glut he describes, the honest competitive position is that content is abundant and free, and the paid product's differentiator is adherence. The rep understood this instinctively and sold accountability rather than programming, which is why it worked — but he never priced the difference explicitly, which is what the household conversation later needed.

anchors.raw: she thinks it's more than our house payment monthly
anchors.note: The decisive anchor, and it came from the person holding the money rather than the person on the call. It reframes $6,000 as a recurring household obligation rather than a one-off investment. It is also precisely the anchor a 50/50 or monthly structure is designed to dismantle, and no structure was offered. Recorded as the clearest instance in the batch of an anchor that the existing payment-plan policy could have answered and did not.

anchors.raw: She thinks I can just learn the information by myself, pretty much.
anchors.note: Materially strengthened by the fact that it is partly true — he holds a physical therapy assistant degree and volunteered 'I know a lot of anatomy stuff'. The correct rebuttal is the one he made himself, that the gap is not knowledge but structure and accountability, and it was never carried back to the person who raised it.

anchors.raw: I have a 5,000 limit on my credit card, and that's sitting at zero. So I'll get my, I think she has better credit and she has a bigger credit card.
anchors.note: A hard ceiling below the asking price, stated unprompted, and the moment the deal's dependence on his wife became structural rather than social. It passed without any acknowledgement. Later confirmed as total dependence: 'we have one bank account it all goes into hers.'

anchors.raw: I have a 35 pound kettlebell and a 40 pound kettlebell, but like the 35 is what I started with.
anchors.note: Equipment already owned and matching the recommended starting weight, which the rep used well: 'The good thing is we recommend most people to start with a 35. So you've already got the equipment too.' Removes friction and start-up cost from the decision.

unmet_demand.want: Community and camaraderie — being part of a group of driven people, which he named three separate times and identified as missing from his whole life
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme does appear to have a community component — the Skool group referenced in the playbook's onboarding steps — and it was never mentioned on this call. What he was offered instead was one-to-one asynchronous access to Trevor plus the rep personally. His stated need is explicitly not one-to-one: 'I wasn't around sports, wasn't around the sense of camaraderie and driving each other up... I'm looking for that' and 'every time Trevor's videos pop up I just wish I could be part of that.' The product plausibly serves this and nobody said so.

unmet_demand.want: A payment structure a single-income household with a new baby could absorb without exceeding its monthly mortgage cost
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No payment plan was offered on this call. The 50% down with the balance inside 90 days that this same rep structured for two other prospects forty-eight hours earlier would have directly answered the objection actually raised. The prospect was instead routed to a lump sum on an account he does not control.

unmet_demand.want: Support with what he repeatedly framed as a mental rather than physical problem — 'it's more of a mental thing for me, like I really do, like I feel like I'm mentally stuck'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is training, nutrition and mobility. The rep engaged the psychological material at length and skilfully, but what was actually sold does not include any mental health provision, and the prospect's own theory of his problem is psychological with childhood-trauma content attached. Whether coaching accountability resolves this is genuinely unknown and should not be assumed.
